resources.string: How delta cells tune the islet
Educational model of normal adult human islet signaling. Cell positions, motion, and signal traces are schematic, not measured or personal data.
A delta cell among its neighbors
Delta cells make somatostatin. Human islets can contain intermixed delta, alpha, and beta cells. The neighbors shown are an example, not a fixed cell arrangement.
Released somatostatin can reach nearby cells within the same islet. This short-range communication is called paracrine signaling.
Somatostatin can reduce glucagon release from alpha cells and insulin release from beta cells. The response depends on other signals each cell receives.
Dampening is not an off switch
The two moving traces illustrate smaller changes in release, not measured concentrations. Local feedback tunes secretion rather than forcing either hormone to zero.

Pancreatic polypeptide: an islet signal in blood
Educational model of normal adult human digestive signaling. Routes, timing, and particle counts are schematic, not measured or personal data.
PP cells make pancreatic polypeptide (PP). These cells are especially concentrated in the uncinate process, a part of the pancreatic head. They are not confined to that region.
Digestive signals during a meal can prompt PP cells to release more pancreatic polypeptide. The food itself does not enter the PP cells.
The cells release PP into nearby blood vessels. The blood carries it beyond the islet; PP does not travel through the pancreatic duct as a digestive enzyme.
Circulating PP can help modulate digestive activity, including the output of pancreatic enzymes. It is one of several signals and does not switch digestion on or off.

Thyroid C cells: calcitonin and bone minerals
Educational model of normal adult human mineral physiology. Tissue, motion, and particles are schematic, not measured or personal data.
Parafollicular cells, also called C cells, lie in the outer part of the follicular wall or between thyroid follicles. They do not face the colloid-filled lumen.
A rise in blood calcium can stimulate C cells to release calcitonin into the blood. This is distinct from thyroid hormone production by follicular cells.
Calcitonin can reduce the activity of osteoclasts, the cells that resorb bone. This can slow the release of calcium from the bone surface.
A supporting role in mineral balance

In adults, parathyroid hormone and active vitamin D are the main regulators of blood calcium, acting across bone, kidneys, and gut. Calcitonin can affect bone resorption but usually plays a smaller role in everyday blood calcium balance.
Parathyroid hormone and active vitamin D
Adrenal cortex: three layers, different hormones
Educational model of normal adult human adrenal cortex. Layer sizes, motion, and hormone symbols are schematic, not measured or personal data.
A connective tissue capsule covers the gland. The cortex has three zones under the capsule and around the inner medulla. The medulla is not part of the cortex.
In the zona glomerulosa, cells form small clusters beneath the capsule. This zone produces mineralocorticoids, chiefly aldosterone, which helps the kidneys regulate salt and water balance.
The zona fasciculata has long cords of cells. This zone makes glucocorticoids, chiefly cortisol in humans, which helps regulate metabolism and responses to stress.
The zona reticularis, next to the medulla, has a network of cell cords. It mainly makes adrenal androgen precursors such as DHEA, which other tissues can convert to more active hormones.

Steroid hormones from all three cortical zones enter nearby blood channels and travel beyond the gland. The symbols identify typical products; they do not show amounts or imply that every zone makes only one product.
